items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: my cousin, he used to work as a dishwasher under my daddy. They called him Cloppy.

ctx.x: And my dad was just like, he was French, but he had this, like Italian, and you couldn't tell him from French, you couldn't tell him from Italian, but he's French. Yeah. His mother was French, I suppose. And, well, of course, it was all jubileed up. Yeah. Well, so when he went to street, it's all right. Just like anything else, well, they'll pass over him, like they pass over a lot of people in the streets now. You can't tell who's who these days in time. Yes. That's right. That's what I said. We ought to be…

Yeah. The only word must have been worse at that time. It's his voice. Do you remember, if I remember rightly, Big Eye Louie, you know, Louie Nelson, the clarinet player, I think said his father was killed in that riot. Do you remember? Did he ever tell you anything about it? Well, I didn't know Louie's father, whatever. I didn't know him. I don't know what. I mean, did Louie ever tell you anything about it?
